history.summary: CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name - this temple is in KARNATAKA (town Aihole), not the value shown in the CSV. One of the oldest structural temples in India, south of the Durga temple at Aihole. DATING CONFLICT: older sources date it 7th-8th century, but current scholarship (incl. Wikipedia) places it about the 5th century (~450 CE). Built in a Panchayatana-like early experimental style adapted from wooden construction in stone - starts rectangular, ends square, with a steep roof, flat roof, and no shikhara originally (a damaged Nagara shikhara over the centre appears to be a later addition). Mukha mandapa of 12 carved pillars, sabha mandapa pillars in two concentric squares, lattice windows in north-Indian style, floral wall patterns. Originally dedicated to Vishnu (Garuda on the sanctum lintel), it later housed a Shiva linga and Nandi, and was also used as a Surya Narayana shrine. Named after Lad Khan, who turned it into his residence during a military campaign - sources conflict on whether he was an Adil Shahi general or a 'Muslim prince' (verify). ASI-protected monument.

name: Lad Khan Temple
town_description: Aihole in Bagalkot district, Karnataka, was an early Chalukya capital and is called the 'cradle of Indian temple architecture' for its 100+ experimental 6th-12th century temples. Together with Badami and Pattadakal it forms the Chalukyan architectural triangle; the Lad Khan temple stands in the main Durga temple complex by the Malaprabha river.
